units.text: INT. SEAGULL - CONTINUOUS
It must be lunch-time.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: She walks away languidly, with a dragging step.
My foot has gone to sleep.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: She is going to have a couple of drinks before lunch.
units.name: DORN

units.text: The poor soul is unhappy.
units.name: SORIN

units.text: That is a trifle, your honour.
units.name: DORN

units.text: You judge her like a man who has obtained all he wants in life.
units.name: SORIN

units.text: Oh, what could be duller than this dear tedium of the country? The air is hot and still, nobody does anything but sit and philosophise about life. It is pleasant, my friends, to sit and listen to you here, but I had rather a thousand times sit alone in the room of a hotel learning a role by heart.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: With enthusiasm.
You are quite right. I understand how you feel.
units.name: NINA

units.text: Of course it is pleasanter to live in town. One can sit in one’s library with a telephone at one’s elbow, no one comes in without being first announced by the footman, the streets are full of cabs, and all---
units.name: SORIN

units.text: Sings.
“Tell her, oh flowers---”
SHAMRAEFF comes in, followed by PAULINA.
Here they are. How do you do?
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: He kisses ARKADINA’S hand and then NINA’S.
I am delighted to see you looking so well.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: To ARKADINA.
My wife tells me that you mean to go to town with her to-day. Is that so?
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: Yes, that is what I had planned to do.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Hm--that is splendid, but how do you intend to get there, madam? We are hauling rye to-day, and all the men are busy. What horses would you take?
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: What horses? How do I know what horses we shall have?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: Why, we have the carriage horses.
units.name: SORIN

units.text: The carriage horses! And where am I to find the harness for them? This is astonishing! My dear madam, I have the greatest respect for your talents, and would gladly sacrifice ten years of my life for you, but I cannot let you have any horses to-day.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: But if I must go to town? What an extraordinary state of affairs!
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: You do not know, madam, what it is to run a farm.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: In a burst of anger.
That is an old story! Under these circumstances I shall go back to Moscow this very day. Order a carriage for me from the village, or I shall go to the station on foot.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: losing his temper.
Under these circumstances I resign my position. You must find yourself another manager.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: He goes out.
It is like this every summer: every summer I am insulted here. I shall never set foot here again.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She goes out to the left, in the direction of the wharf.
In a few minutes she is seen entering the house, followed by TRIGORIN, who carries a bucket and fishing-rod.
Losing his temper.
What the deuce did he mean by his impudence? I want all the horses brought here at once!
units.name: SORIN

units.text: To PAULINA.
How could he refuse anything to Madame Arkadina, the famous actress? Is not every wish, every caprice even, of hers, more important than any farm work? This is incredible.
units.name: NINA

units.text: In despair.
What can I do about it? Put yourself in my place and tell me what I can do.
units.name: PAULINA

units.text: To NINA.
Let us go and find my sister, and all beg her not to go.
units.name: SORIN

units.text: He looks in the direction in which SHAMRAEFF went out.
That man is insufferable; a regular tyrant.
units.name: SORIN

units.text: Preventing him from getting up.
Sit still, sit still, and let us wheel you.
units.name: NINA
